title: Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, and suppose that $g$ is the Gaussian generator of $f$ in the sense that both functions are square-integrable for standard Gaussian product measure and the corresponding Gaussian noise difference quotients converge to $g$ in $L^2$ as the positive time parameter tends to zero. If $f$ is three times continuously differentiable, then
\[
\operatorname{Ent}_\gamma(f^2)\le 2\int_{\mathbb R^n}\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(Df(x)[e_i]\bigr)^2\,d\gamma(x),
\]
where $\gamma$ is standard Gaussian product measure and $e_i$ is the $i$th coordinate vector.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ and $g$ are square-integrable for standard Gaussian product measure
$g$ is the $L^2$ limit of the positive-time Gaussian noise difference quotients of $f$
